one_liner: Pure-Rust libxml2 reimplementation: parsing at libxml2 parity, self-reported 1.5-2.4x faster serialization and 1.1-2.7x faster XPath.
what_it_does: A memory-safe Rust rewrite of libxml2's feature set: XML 1.0 DOM parsing with error recovery, SAX2, XmlReader and push APIs, XPath 1.0 plus some 2.0 functions, DTD/RelaxNG/XSD/Schematron validation, C14N, XInclude, XML catalogs, HTML 4.01 and WHATWG HTML5 parsers, CSS selectors, and an xmllint clone. The Rust API is its own design (a Document addressed by NodeId indices, plus free functions such as xpath::evaluate and serial::serialize), not libxml2's. For C/C++ users, a C FFI (xmloxide.h) and a libxml2_compat.h shim map common libxml2 calls onto opaque handles. The README reports 1727/1727 W3C conformance tests and 119/119 libxml2 regression tests passing.
how_it_is_fast: The DOM is an arena: one Vec<NodeData> indexed by NonZeroU32 NodeIds with parent, first/last-child and sibling links. Serialization is a single pre-order walk that pushes into one String with a char-by-char escaper. The parser is hand-written recursive descent over UTF-8 bytes, with scalar bulk scans for text and attribute values, ASCII fast paths for names and built-in entities, and a byte pre-check for invalid characters; it uses no SIMD and no memchr. XPath fuses a `//` step and the child step after it into one descendant step, inlines name tests on the child and descendant axes, and short-circuits literal positional predicates. The README also claims string interning, but the tree does not use it: element names, prefixes and namespace URIs are owned Strings, and the Dict/SymbolId interner is referenced only in src/util/dict.rs.
when_to_use: Rust (or C via the FFI) code that needs libxml2's breadth — validation, XPath, C14N, XInclude, catalogs, HTML — without linking the C library, which the README says has been unmaintained since December 2025.
Serialization-heavy pipelines (parse or build a DOM, then emit XML), where the README shows 1.5-2.4x faster output than libxml2 on 4.9-374 KB documents.
Parsing many independent documents across threads: there is no global init or state, and Document is Send + Sync.
Parsing XML and WHATWG HTML5 (100% of html5lib-tests) through one crate and one tree API; libxml2 has no HTML5 parser.
Workloads where parse speed only needs to match libxml2: parsing is 0.89-1.12x libxml2's speed on the project's own fixtures.
when_not_to_use: When raw parse throughput is the goal: 4 of 5 README parse benchmarks are 3-13% slower than libxml2, and faster Rust parsers exist.
Truly incremental parsing of large inputs: PushParser buffers all pushed data and parses only on finish(). Use SAX instead.
Evaluating untrusted XPath expressions: open issue #51 reports that a few thousand nested parentheses overflow the stack and abort the process in 0.5.0.

RelaxNG-heavy validation: issues #52-#57 are open (<div> not traversed, combine= ignored for same-named defines, prefixed-name shorthand not resolved, attributes behind <ref> in interleave never matched, no compact syntax).
XML 1.1, XSLT, custom entity loaders, custom error handlers, or code that dereferences libxml2 node structs: none of these are supported.

integration.form: crate (also a cdylib/staticlib through the Makefile with the `ffi` feature; the repo also has Python (PyO3) and WASM subcrates)
integration.dependencies: encoding_rs only for the library. The default `cli` feature pulls in clap, so library users should set default-features = false. Optional: serde, tokio (async), libxml (benchmarks only).
integration.platforms: Any Rust target as far as documented. The code is pure Rust and the parser scanner has no architecture-specific or SIMD paths; a WASM bindings subcrate exists.
integration.thread_safety: No global state; Document is Send + Sync and mutation needs &mut Document. The FFI keeps its last-error state in thread-local storage. MIGRATION.md says a document shared across threads needs a mutex.
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — the C FFI plus libxml2_compat.h maps common libxml2 names (xmlReadMemory, xmlDocGetRootElement, xmlXPathEval, ...). Nodes are opaque (doc, id) handles, so there is no node->name or node->children access. Every handle and returned string must be freed, and there are no parser contexts, error handlers or entity loaders. The Rust API is not libxml2-shaped.

gotchas: XPath name tests ignore namespaces unless you register prefixes. An unprefixed test like //entry matches on local name only (the matches_element_name fallback), so it finds Atom-namespaced <entry> elements where libxml2 and XPath 1.0 return an empty set. Namespace-sensitive queries ported from libxml2 can return different results.

Inferred from reading src/xpath/eval.rs, not run: try_fuse_descendant_child rewrites descendant-or-self::node()/child::X[pred] into descendant::X[pred] and copies the predicates unconditionally. //b[1] therefore looks like it returns only the first b in the document, not the first b child of each parent; XPath 1.0 §2.5 notes that //para[1] is not /descendant::para[1].

Default ParseOptions limits: nesting depth 256, 256 attributes per element, 10 MB per text node or attribute value, and 10,000 entity expansions. Large or unusual documents need these raised explicitly.

The API is pre-1.0 and changing. In 0.5.0 XPathValue::NodeSet switched to XPathNode entries, attribute paths stopped collapsing to String, and a new Expr::FilterPath variant was added. Use ≥0.5.0 anyway: 0.4.4 fixed CVE-2026-61727 (stack overflow from nested DTD content models), and 0.5.0 fixed an exponential-time entity recursion check.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick xmloxide over quick-xml or SupXML when you need libxml2's whole feature set (validation, XPath, C14N, XInclude, HTML4/HTML5, SAX/reader/push, C FFI) in safe Rust rather than raw speed: SupXML reports ~2.1x libxml2's DOM parse speed and quick-xml leads the bemayer benchmark, while xmloxide only matches libxml2 at parsing. Compared with rusty_xml, the other Rust libxml2 remake (1.55-2.31x on xmllint parse-noout), xmloxide's speed case rests on serialization and XPath, not parsing.
verified_claims_summary: The project's own Criterion benchmarks compare against libxml2 through the Rust libxml crate (0.3.8 in Cargo.lock), built with thin LTO and codegen-units=1; CPU, rustc and libxml2 versions are not stated, and the README numbers date from 2026-02-28, before 0.1.0, and were not re-run for 0.5.0. They show parsing at 0.89-1.12x libxml2 on five 4.9-374 KB documents, serialization 1.5-2.4x faster, and XPath 1.08-2.7x faster. The libxml2 side of the serialization benchmark adds xmlSaveToBuffer plus a CStr-to-String lossy copy. The XPath queries are unprefixed names on default-namespaced Atom and POM fixtures, so under XPath 1.0 rules libxml2 matches nothing while xmloxide matches by local name; the benchmark never checks that both sides return the same results.
status_note: Actively released: more than a dozen crates.io versions from 0.1.x (2026-03-01) to 0.5.0 (2026-08-08), about 57k downloads and 4 reverse dependencies. It is MIT-licensed, maintained by a single author with an AI coding agent (the repo carries CLAUDE.md and .claude/skills), and still pre-1.0 with recent breaking XPath changes.
